book.title: Purchasing Whiteness: Pardos, Mulattos, and the Quest for Social Mobility in the Spanish Indies

evidence: academic press signal: Stanford University Press / Stanford University Press
academic press signal: Stanford University Press / Stanford University Press

argument.statement: In the Spanish Indies, petitioners could pursue social mobility and escape casta discrimination by purchasing whiteness via a royal gracias al sacar exemption granting privileges of Whiteness.

book.rationale: The book primarily explores the racial dynamics and social mobility within the context of the casta system in colonial Spanish America, categorizing it chiefly under Race & Ethnicity while also reflecting elements of American History and societal context.
book.summary: The colonization of Spanish America resulted in the mixing of Natives, Europeans, and Africans and the subsequent creation of a casta system that discriminated against them. Members of mixed races could, however, free themselves from such burdensome restrictions through the purchase of a gracias al sacar—a royal exemption that provided the privileges of Whiteness. For more than a century, the whitening gracias al sacar has fascinated historians. Even while the documents remained elusive, scholars continually mentioned the potential to acquire Whiteness as a provocative marker of the historic differences between Anglo and Latin American treatments of race. Purchasing Whiteness explores the fascinating details of 40 cases of whitening petitions, tracking thousands of pages of ensuing conversations as petitioners, royal officials, and local elites disputed not only whether the state should grant full whiteness to deserving individuals, but whether selective prejudices against the castas should cease. Purchasing Whiteness contextualizes the history of the gracias al sacar within the broader framework of three centuries of mixed race efforts to end discrimination.
